# Contract: Module Translations

**Feature**: `019-localization-language-packs` | **Binding modules**: `gp-module/`, `modules/build.sh`, `operator/internal/oci`, `operator/internal/modsrc`, `operator/internal/controller` (Module reconciler), `api/internal/handlers/modules.go`, `api/internal/handlers/module_upload.go` | **Status**: Binding

## 1. Ids (derived from module.yaml / template.yaml; generated by `gp-module i18n extract`)

| Id | Source field |
|---|---|
| `module.displayName`, `module.summary` | `module.yaml` |
| `template.displayName`, `template.description` | `template.yaml spec` |
| `versions.<id>.displayName` | version picker entries |
| `config.<key>.displayName`, `config.<key>.description`, `config.<key>.options.<value>` | configuration fields |
| `actions.<id>.displayName`, `actions.<id>.description`, `actions.<id>.group` | console actions |
| `actions.<id>.params.<name>.displayName`, `….description`, `….options.<value>` | action params |
| `mods.<volume>.displayName` | mod volumes |
| `metrics.<id>.displayName` | metrics |

Ids use the YAML identifiers with a reversible escape (JSON Pointer style): `~` → `~0`, then `.` → `~1`. So `a.b` becomes `a~1b` and `a~b` becomes `a~0b`; unescaping applies `~1` → `.` then `~0` → `~`. Commands, regexes, env values and images are never translatable.

**Module id rule.** A module id is one of the fixed prefixes `module`, `template`, `versions`, `config`, `actions`, `mods`, `metrics` followed by dot-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9_~-]`, where `~` appears only as the escapes `~0` and `~1`:

```text
^(module|template|versions|config|actions|mods|metrics)(\.[A-Za-z0-9_~-]+)+$
```

Upper case is allowed because ids embed names from the YAML (for example `config.MAX_PLAYERS.displayName`). Dashboard and server ids keep the strict lower-case regex in [data-model.md](../data-model.md). The shared derivation and the rule live in `i18n/modlocale` (`Derive`, `ValidID`); `gp-module i18n extract`, `i18n-check --module` and the operator all use it. Open risk: a YAML identifier or enum value containing a space, `/`, `:` or `+` yields an id outside the character set; see OPEN-DECISIONS.md (OD-007).

Module translations carry `sourceHash` like app packs: the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the English text, written by `gp-module i18n stamp`. A changed English text makes the entry `needs-review` (still shown; `gp-module validate` warns with rule `locale-needs-review`).

## 2. Packaging (all module sources)

Each `locales/<tag>.json` reaches the operator through every module source, with the same file names and the same validation. `en.json` is never shipped (the template is the default text).

| Source | How a translation travels |
|---|---|
| OCI | one layer per file: media type `application/vnd.gameplane.module.locale.v1+json`, title annotation `locales/<tag>.json`; a layer over 900 KiB is recorded as oversized, not dropped |
| directory, local, git, HTTP archive (tar.gz / zip) | the file `locales/<tag>.json` in the module directory |
| upload | ConfigMap key `locales.<tag>.json` (a key cannot contain `/`); the API copies `locales/<tag>.json` from the uploaded archive and counts the bytes against the bundle limit |
| `gp-module package --output` tar.gz | contains `locales/<tag>.json` (so it works as an HTTP or upload source) |

Pushed to OCI by `modules/build.sh` and `gp-module package`. Cosign covers OCI layers through the manifest signature (FR-033); the other sources have no signature (existing behavior). Bundles without locale files stay valid.

## 3. Operator

The Module reconciler (the GameTemplate reconciler never sees the bundle) validates each locale file with `i18n/pack` against ids derived from the bundled `module.yaml` and `template.yaml` on install/upgrade. Valid entries go to ConfigMap `<template>-locales` (`data["<tag>.json"]`) in the operator namespace, the namespace Gameplane runs in (`--module-namespace`); the GameTemplate is cluster-scoped, so the owner reference points at a cluster-scoped owner. Invalid entries are dropped. Module install never fails because of locales (FR-034).

Condition `LocalesValid`:

| Reason | Status | When |
|---|---|---|
| `Valid` | True | every translation is valid; message "All module translations are valid." |
| `InvalidEntries` | False | entries or whole files were dropped |
| `LocalesTooLarge` | False | a language is over the size limit or the languages together exceed it |
| `WriteFailed` | False | the ConfigMap could not be written; retried after a minute |

Priority when several apply: `WriteFailed` > `LocalesTooLarge` > `InvalidEntries` > `Valid`.

Size bounds: one file is read up to 900 KiB (a hard memory cap); a larger file reaches the reconciler as an "oversized" language tag, is never stored, and makes `LocalesTooLarge`. All locale files of one bundle together are read up to 4 MiB (`oci.MaxLocaleTotalSize`), counted in file-name order (OCI layers by title annotation, directories by file name, so `pt-BR.json` sorts before `pt.json`); a language that would push the running total over the budget is recorded as oversized like an oversized file and is not read, while a later, smaller language can still fit. This applies to the OCI and directory-based sources (directory, local, git, HTTP archive); uploads stay bounded by the 900 KiB bundle limit. The ConfigMap data for all languages together MUST stay ≤ 900 KiB (below the 1 MiB Kubernetes limit): languages are added in tag order until the next one would exceed the bound; the rest are left out. The language tags of both kinds appear in the condition message and in the Warning event, and those languages fall back to the template's default text.

Events: Warning events `InvalidLocaleEntries` (up to 20 `tag:id: problem` lines, note capped at 1024 bytes), `LocalesTooLarge` and `LocalesWriteFailed` fire only when the problem list changes, tracked by the annotation `gameplane.local/locales-problems` (a fingerprint) on the GameTemplate, not on every re-pull. A failed write counts as one problem whatever its error text, so the one-minute retries do not repeat events; a failed delete of stale translations also reports `WriteFailed`.

## 4. API

`GET /api/v1/modules/{name}/locales/{tag}` (mounted in the existing `/modules` route group, `api/internal/handlers/modules.go`) → `200 {"<id>": "<ICU message string>"}`: the validated message text exactly as stored (the dashboard formats it; the API never compiles it). Resolution `tag` → base language → `{}`. A malformed or unknown tag, a module with no translations and a missing ConfigMap all return `200 {}`; `404` only when the module does not exist. Requires `modules:read`, the same RBAC as `GET /api/v1/modules/{name}`.

## 5. Dashboard

Create-server and server-settings screens look up module ids in the fetched locale map, fall back to the template's own text (FR-032).
